text:
Alex (Sales): heads-up — enterprise prospect (FinServ firm) asked for a proposal: reserved capacity + a pool of prepaid "credits" that can be burned for burst overages. wants a single blended price and clear overage mechanics. can product weigh in on acceptable packaging?
Emily (Product): thanks. couple quick Qs: 1) expected committed GPUs / qps? 2) typical seq lengths & embedding vs generation split? 3) contract term they're asking for?
Alex (Sales): they proposed 12mo, commit = 8 A100-equivalent units (steady), peaks up to ~20 for short windows. mostly generation, 70% chat-like with avg seq ~512 tokens. embeddings for search are small portion (~5%).
Sara (FinOps): from margin side we need blended rate floor. if we do credits, what is redemption rate? e.g. 1 credit = 1k tokens or 1 credit = 1 model-hour? need to map to unit economics.
Matt (Eng): technical: if we guarantee 8 GPUs reserved, bursts to 20 will require either autoscaling burst capacity or routing to hosted non-dedicated pool. do we promise latency SLO for burst traffic? that's important for canary/fallback logic.
Kevin (Solutions): client also wants the ability to reserve a fraction for compliance workloads (on-prem enclave). can we support hybrid routing where reserved pool is private but overage credits hit hosted?
Emily (Product): proposed approach: - Offer "Reserved + Burst Credits" SKU: base monthly commit (8 GPU-equivalent) + prepaid credit bucket sold in packs that map to compute units. - Redemption mapping: 1 credit pack = 100k gen tokens (~approx cost-backed) — open to calibration. - SLA: keep base commit SLOs; burst best-effort with priority routing and fallbacks. need legal to sign off on SLA language.
Sara (FinOps): ballpark pricing thought: base reserved price = our standard dedicated rate * 0.92 (discount for commit), credit pack markup should cover expected tail usage cost + 15% margin. we'll build a P&L once we fix redemption mapping.
Alex (Sales): client will push for a true blended per-token headline. can we provide an "effective per-token" example for a 12mo contract with X credit packs? they want a single # to present to procurement.
Matt (Eng): we can generate an example calc but must add caveat about latency/availability differences when served from hosted burst. also note that quantized variants might be used in burst path which could slightly change quality. need product decision if quality parity required.
Emily (Product): launch criteria (what product needs before committing): 1) defined redemption mapping & sample pricing sheet; 2) documented fallback behavior & customer-facing SLA bullets; 3) infra readiness signoff: burst routing + capacity pool config; 4) handoff playbook for support + solutions. if any of those are missing, we'll label as "pilot-only".
Kevin (Solutions): for the hybrid ask, we can do flow: private reserved for committed traffic, credits route to hosted public pool with dedicated priority tag. we'll need clear data transfer and audit trail docs. ops impact is medium.
Sara (FinOps): action for me: i'll produce a sensitivity table (per-token effective price) with commit sizes 4/8/16 and credit pack sizes. ETA EOD Thurs.
Emily (Product): action items: - Sara to produce sensitivity table - Matt to document fallback/quality delta & infra constraints - Kevin to draft hybrid routing diagram - Alex to get customer expected monthly burn range. we'll reassess after those. tagging @triage-bot to create product backlog ticket.
triage-bot: created ticket PROD-1428 "enterprise: reserved + burst credits pricing proposal" assigned to Emily (Product). priority: P2.
Alex (Sales): thanks all — I'll push for the monthly burn numbers and loop in procurement. :thumbsup:
Emily (Product): ok. if we can provide a concrete sample quote next week we can move to proposal stage. otherwise pilot only.
Matt (Eng): FYI: if client insists on strict latency for bursts, cost jumps ~30% because we need warmed instances in multiple regions. calling that out now.
Sara (FinOps): noted. I'll include that uplift in the sensitivity table.
Alex (Sales): copying in customer contact in DM, will update here when they confirm.
Emily (Product): cool — thanks team.
